articles.title: Marcoleta suspended for 90 days over plunder charges
articles.summary: The Sandiganbayan Third Division has ordered the preventive suspension of Sen. Rodante Marcoleta from his post as a senator due to plunder charges.

blocks.text: October 19, 2026 | 6:08pm
Senator Rodante Marcoleta boards a Philippine National Police coaster at the Sandiganbayan on Monday, July 6, 2026, upon his arrest over a plunder case.
The STAR / Michael Varcas
MANILA, Philippines — The Sandiganbayan Third Division has ordered the preventive suspension of Sen. Rodante Marcoleta from his post as a senator due to plunder charges.
In a resolution penned by Justice Karl Miranda and promulgated on October 19, the anti-graft court ordered Marcoleta suspended for 90 days, effective upon his receipt of the resolution.
The suspension will automatically be lifted once the 90-day period expires, according to the anti-graft court.
The suspension stemmed from two separate cases filed against the lawmaker involving plunder and an alleged violation of Presidential Decree (P.D.) No. 46.

According to the charges, during his tenure as the SAGIP Party-List representative, Marcoleta allegedly amassed P75 million in ill-gotten wealth, which he did not declare in his Statement of Contributions and Expenditures.
He allegedly received the donations from his co-accused, former lawmaker Mike Defensor and businessman Aristotle Viray.

In its resolution, the anti-graft court explained that under Republic Act (R.A.) No. 7080, or the Plunder Law, and R.A. No. 3019, or the Anti-Graft and Corrupt Practices Act, preventive suspension is mandatory once a valid Information has been established.
The anti-graft court noted that there is no requirement for a pre-suspension hearing for plunder under its Internal Rules or existing jurisprudence.

“Considering that the Information has been determined to be valid, it becomes the ministerial duty of the Court to forthwith issue the order of preventive suspension. The Court has neither the discretion nor duty to determine whether or not a preventive suspension is required. There are no ifs and buts about it,” the anti-graft court said.

The anti-graft court maintained that a plain reading of the factual allegations in the Informations, if hypothetically admitted, sufficiently establishes the elements of plunder and violation of P.D. No. 46.
The Sandiganbayan also assured the public that Marcoleta's suspension will not disrupt the legislative branch.

“Moreover, the preventive suspension of Sen. Marcoleta will not affect the functions of the Senate. The Senate, a collegial body composed of 24 Senators, can still perform its functions even during the preventive suspension of a member. The Senate committees may also continue to perform their tasks through their remaining members,” the anti-graft court said.
On October 12, the anti-graft court also imposed a 90-day suspension on Sen. Jinggoy Estrada due to plunder charges.

articles.title: Hurricane Trudy menaces Mexico’s Pacific coast and Greece hit by deadly floods
articles.summary:
Trudy weakens to tropical storm after warnings of strong winds and heavy rain, while one person killed in Greece

In contrast to the quiet Atlantic hurricane season, the Pacific has seen…
articles.byline: Alice Nightingale-Smith and Nick Lee for MetDesk

blocks.text: In contrast to the quiet Atlantic hurricane season, there has been ongoing activity in the Pacific, with Trudy being the 22nd and latest named system. The category 2 hurricane remained roughly 100 miles (160km) south-west of the coast of Mexico, meaning the worst of the conditions stayed offshore. However, the US National Hurricane Center put coastal parts of the states of Jalisco, Michoacán and Colima under hurricane warnings, with sustained winds of up to 60-90mph forecast on Sunday.

Rainfall totals of 100-150mm were likely for these areas, prompting warnings of flooding and landslides. Warnings also covered the risk of a dangerous storm surge accompanied by damaging waves in areas of onshore winds across the coast of south-western Mexico. By Monday morning, Trudy had weakened and been downgraded to a tropical storm, with coastal warnings being lifted.

In Greece, heavy rain and thunderstorms caused severe flooding and one fatality across Rhodes, Evia and the Sporades islands last week. According to the National Observatory of Athens, a station in Rhodes recorded 202mm between 3.30am and 9.50am (UTC) on 14 October. Regional authorities reported more than 30 rescue and extrication operations in response to flooding, while the Greek coastguard said four passenger vehicles were swept into the sea during the storm. On Skiathos, flood waters swept away two cars.

blocks.caption: Cars swept into the sea on the Greek island of Rhodes. Photograph: Kyriakos Finas/Reuters

blocks.text: Five deaths were reported due to severe flooding in Istanbul, Turkey, last week. Heavy rain on 14 and 15 October prompted school closures, flight delays, disruptive flooding and landslides across several provinces. According to the Istanbul metropolitan municipality, 242mm of rain was recorded in Beykoz, a district of Istanbul province. Nearly 600 people were rescued after becoming stranded and at least 2,700 people were forced to evacuate their homes.

The Turkish state meteorological service issued further alerts for heavy rain and thunderstorms over the weekend across dozens of provinces, with at least an additional 40-60mm forecast for parts of the Marmara and western Black Sea regions.

articles.title: PNP-CIDG subpoenas 21 individuals over attempted Laos drug shipment
articles.summary: The Philippine National Police"s Criminal Investigation and Detection Group (PNP-CIDG) has summoned 21 individuals to give information regarding the attempted shipment of 521 kilograms of shabu from…

blocks.text: Published October 19, 2026 6:06pm

The Philippine National Police’s Criminal Investigation and Detection Group (PNP-CIDG) has summoned 21 individuals to give information regarding the attempted shipment of 521 kilograms of shabu from Laos.
According to Isa Avendaño-Umali’s report in Super Radyo dzBB, PNP spokesperson Col. Allen Rae Co said that he wants the summoned individuals to speak about their side.
Co reportedly said that most of the subpoenaed individuals have already gone to the PNP-CIDG.
Meanwhile, there could be more individuals to be summoned regarding the matter according to Co, the report said.
The PNP spokesperson, however, clarified that being subpoenaed over the issue does not mean that they are dealing with illegal drugs.

Interior Secretary Jonvic Remulla on Friday identified the Mindanao politician allegedly involved in the attempted smuggling of P3.5 billion worth of shabu from Laos to the Philippines as former Bangsamoro Parliament member Edriezan Hadji Nasser Rimbang.

Remulla said this at a Palace briefing as he presented a link diagram of the individuals allegedly involved in the planned smuggling of 521 kilograms of suspected methamphetamine hydrochloride or shabu.
But Rimbang has yet to make a comment on the matter.

Remulla said Rimbang allegedly paid Police Master Sergeant Aileen Jane Manalo Mendoza for the landing rights and the private hangar where the plane was supposed to land from Laos in the last week of September.
The private plane, Remulla said, was allegedly procured by Captain Rioklyn Toledo alias "Boyet" from Malaysia to Laos. — Vince Angelo Ferreras/RSJ, GMA News

articles.title: Australian MP seriously hurt in suspected car attack
articles.summary: Helen Haines, an independent federal lawmaker, has been struck by a car in what Australia's prime minister has called an apparent attack.

image.caption: Helen Haines was elected to the Australian parliament in 2019Image: Mick Tsikas/AAP Image/AP Photo/picture alliance

blocks.text: Australian police are investigating a suspected car attack that has left independent MP Helen Haines with critical injuries.
Counterterrorism investigators have joined the probe following the incident, which occurred outside Haines' constituency office in Wangaratta, northeast of the Victorian capital, Melbourne.
What do we know about the suspected attack on Haines?
Haines, 65, was hit by an SUV, said by police to be a white Toyota, outside her office, leaving her with serious injuries, particularly to her lower body.
The driver, described as a 43-year-old man, has been arrested, according to Prime Minister Anthony Albanese.
Investigators are reported to have found a knife in the car.

blocks.caption: Prime Minister Albanese has said the incident seemed 'no accident'Image: Marek Ladzinski/ZUMA/picture alliance

blocks.text: Apparently deliberate attack: PM Albanese
"This wasn't an accident. There was a deliberate act, it would appear," Albanese told broadcaster ABC. He said it was too early to speculate about the possible motive behind the attack.
At a separate press conference, Albanese said everyone was "praying for her full recovery."

Although it has not yet been established whether the incident was deliberate, there has been an increase in threats and harassment targeting lawmakers and other senior public officials in Australia and elsewhere in recent years.

articles.title: Marcos pushes to improve nurse-to-patient ratio in PH
articles.summary: President Ferdinand “Bongbong” Marcos Jr. on Monday underscored the need to improve the welfare of Filipino nurses, including by improving nurse-to-patient ratios and providing more opportunities for…

blocks.text: Published October 19, 2026 6:02pm

President Ferdinand “Bongbong” Marcos Jr. on Monday underscored the need to improve the welfare of Filipino nurses, including by improving nurse-to-patient ratios and providing more opportunities for career growth.

Marcos made the statement at the Philippine Nurses Association Inc. (PNA) National Annual Convention 2026 in Pasay City, where he highlighted the contributions of Filipino nurses to the country and the global healthcare workforce.
“Your leaders and all the people that we talked to that are abroad speak of the hard work, the skill, and the dedication that our nurses offer and demonstrate wherever they go," Marcos said.
"I’m very proud to hear this because I know how much our nurses contribute to our country, but also to the countries where they serve,” he added.
The President said the contributions of Filipino nurses deserved the government’s recognition and a sustained commitment to improving their welfare and professional development.

“So, we work very, very hard to strengthen our healthcare system now. We must also work towards improving nurse-to-patient ratios, filling vacant positions, providing more opportunities for our Filipino nurses’ growth,” he said.
“All of this is necessary so that our nurses can carry out responsibilities more efficiently and ensure that our healthcare institutions better serve our people,” Marcos added.

He said his administration was working with the Department of Health (DOH), the Commission on Higher Education (CHED) and the Technical Education and Skills Development Authority (TESDA) to support nurses.
The President also cited the increase in funding for the Health Emergency Allowance, from P6.8 billion in 2022 to more than P110 billion in 2026, for public and private healthcare workers.

The government is also providing employment opportunities and review classes through the Clinical Care Associates Program for nursing graduates who have yet to pass the licensure examination, he said.

“Our goal is to help more qualified Filipinos enter the profession, strengthen the capabilities and protect the welfare of our nurses to ensure that our healthcare institutions have the workforce that they need to serve our communities,” Marcos said.
The President thanked nurses for their hard work and dedicated service.

“Ang inyong husay, ang inyong malasakit, dedikasyon ay patuloy na nagbibigay ng pag-asa sa ating mga kababayan, nagpapalakas sa ating sistemang pangkalusugan. Patuloy po kaming magsisikap upang maibigay ang suporta, benepisyo, at oportunidad na nararapat para sa inyo,” Marcos said.

(Your competence, compassion and dedication continue to give hope to our fellow Filipinos and strengthen our healthcare system. We will continue to strive to provide the support, benefits and opportunities that you deserve.)— MCG, GMA News

articles.title: Ukraine got 'no warning' of Russian ballistic strikes, Zelenskyy says
articles.summary: Massive strikes overnight hit the capital Kyiv, and damaged power stations, killing at least one person and cutting power to hundreds of thousands.

image.caption: The strikes hit Kyiv, including this candy shop in the city centerImage: Efrem Lukatsky/AP Photo/picture alliance

blocks.text: A barrage of Russian ballistic miles struck Kyiv and the surrounding region on Monday, killing at least one person and knocking out power to over half a million homes, Ukrainian authorities said.

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said on Telegram that Russia had launched 16 ballistic missiles, targeting Ukraine's energy facilities, 10 of which were hit, cutting power to some 550,000 households.
The president also lamented the lack of warning from Ukraine's international partners.
"Another Russian ballistic missile attack came in several waves overnight, and once again, there was no early warning from our partners," he wrote.

Ukraine's Air Force reported strikes, which included cruise missiles and drones, hitting 25 locations. Of the 269 recorded Shahed drones deployed in the overnight attack, Ukrainian air defenses reportedly downed or suppressed 243, as well as four missiles.
Ukraine strikes Putin's hometown, as Trump eases pressure on Russia
Moscow says it hit drone, missile hubs in Ukraine
Russia's Defense Ministry also confirmed the "massive strikes" on Monday, saying it had targeted Ukraine with "ground-based high-precision weapons and strike drones."

The ministry said it had hit a Ukrainian data center, a logistics hub storing components for drones and cruise missiles, a train depot storing missiles and an industrial facility involved in the production of drones.
It also said it had struck a bulk carrier in the Black Sea, some 130 kilometers (80 miles) from the port of Odesa, which the ministry said had been carrying military and dual-use cargo.

Ukraine did not confirm those targets but said that a medical facility had been hit in the capital, as well as one of the city's metro stations, according to a post by the Kyiv City Military Administration on Telegram.

blocks.caption: A police officer inspects the site of a fitness club that was hit by a missile Image: Valentyn Ogirenko/REUTERS

blocks.text: Kyiv, Washington disagree over pause to intelligence sharing
The overnight strikes come amid contradictory claims by both Ukraine and the US about pauses to intelligence sharing.
US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said on Monday that Washington had not paused some of its intelligence sharing, denying a statement Zelenskyy made on Sunday.
"I don't know where [Zelenskyy's] getting these things ​or why he's saying these things to the press. You should go back and ask him. There's been no pause," Rubio said during a visit to Uzbekistan.
"What he should ​focus on, and what we want to be focused on, is bringing an end to this war. That's what he should be focused on," he added.
Ukraine is dependent on the ability of US intelligence to spot fast-moving ballistic missiles fired by Russia. Some recent attacks have taken place without warning, Ukrainian officials have reported.
How Trump is helping Putin

articles.title: [Rappler’s Best] And our jaws dropped
articles.summary: The impeachment court is on recess until November 9, when it’s the defense’s turn to present its case. What would the defense’s counter move be?

blocks.text: My apologies for missing last Monday’s newsletter as I took a short break.

This week is the start of the public interviews of five aspirants to the post of chief justice, which will be vacated by Chief Justice Alexander Gesmundo on November 6. He is retiring after over five years since he was appointed by then-president Rodrigo Duterte.

It’s President Ferdinand Marcos Jr.’s first and only chance of choosing the head of the High Tribunal, which is packed with Duterte appointees, before he steps down in 2028. Two of the aspirants, Senior Associate Justice Marvic Leonen and Associate Justice Alfredo Benjamin Caguioa, were appointed to the Court by the late president Noynoy Aquino. The Judicial and Bar Council (JBC) will hold public interviews with both on Thursday, October 22.
The three other aspirants — Duterte appointees associate justices Rodil Zalameda, Japar Dimaampao, and Jose Midas Marquez — will be interviewed by the JBC on October 26.
With a Supreme Court in transition, we can’t expect it to rule on anything that could potentially shuffle the appointing power’s deck of cards.

Which is why, from a purely tactical point of view, it does make sense for the prosecution in the impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte to have made a bombshell bet last week — “all in,” in the words of lead prosecutor Jinky Luistro — by dropping all but one of the four articles of impeachment it lodged against her before the Senate impeachment court.

Unlike last year, when the Court saved the day for the Vice President by barring the first attempt to put her on trial, the defense could feel the winds shifting. “As for certiorari (before the Supreme Court), we are not considering it at this point,” said defense spokesperson Michael Poa in this story.

items: It’s the handwriting on the wall. In August, the SC dismissed two petitions, including one filed by Duterte herself, that questioned the impeachment proceedings against her, saying they were already moot since the trial had already proceeded.

A month later, Duterte lost the second time around, when the justices unanimously dismissed a petition against the Senate court’s decision to adjust the voting threshold to convict the Vice President.

On Day 39 of the trial last week, House prosecutors dropped three complaints against her — misuse of confidential funds, grave threats, and bribery — in a legal maneuver that upset the defense and made lead counsel Sheila Sison bristle with a staccato of qualms and unease. This should not tie our hands, she told the impeachment court.

The prosecution’s move partly stemmed from its reading of the defense’s strategy, which, they say, is to delay the proceedings and bore the public to death. Prosecutors believe they have gained momentum from their latest witness, accountant-lawyer Alex Cabrera, and wanted to go for the kill, so to speak.

Presiding officer Senator Chiz Escudero issued a quick decision that sided with the prosecution, thus retaining just one charge to be judged by the senator-judges: Duterte’s estimated P1.5-billion unexplained wealth, per Cabrera’s numbers.

Who benefits from this situation? In this story, political reporter Dwight de Leon tells us who, plus the fact that timing is already pretty tight, given the 2027 budget that needs to be passed and Manila’s hosting of the ASEAN Summit in mid-November.

blocks.text: For now, the impeachment court is on recess until November 9, when it’s the defense’s turn to present its case. What would the defense’s counter move be? Possibly two things, according to lawyer Lulu Reyes, Rappler’s resident panelist in our coverage of the trial. Watch it here.

items: The defense could seek an outright dismissal of all the articles of impeachment and no longer present its arguments, citing a mistrial.
It could file a demurrer to evidence with the impeachment court, a plea to dismiss the case because the prosecution failed to present sufficient evidence, i.e., Cabrera’s “false assumptions.”

blocks.text: Either way could force an early vote from the senator-judges, according to Reyes.
Truly a sui generis. Spin a win!

articles.title: House lawmakers scoff at Chinese ambassador's remarks, threats of ban
articles.summary: There are grounds to declare Chinese Ambassador Jing Quan persona non grata for his remarks referring to the "use of force" against the Philippines over the West Philippine Sea, House Senior Deputy…

blocks.text: There are grounds to declare Chinese Ambassador Jing Quan persona non grata for his remarks referring to the "use of force" against the Philippines over the West Philippine Sea, House Senior Deputy Minority Leader and ML Party-list Representative Leila de Lima said Monday.

"Unless he apologizes or takes back that remark or that statement, I think the Executive Department should seriously consider declaring him as persona non grata. Kasi he's supposed to be a foreign guest, he's a guest here so he must behave accordingly. Hindi yung palaging harsh ang kanyang mga sinasabi, then threatening, and then hostile yung kanyang demeanor [Not always making harsh remarks, then threatening, and with a hostile demeanour]," de Lima said in an ambush interview.
She also cited China's repeated reference to the Philippines as a "troublemaker" in the region.

"Tayo pa daw ang troublemaker sa lugar natin. Tayo pa ang troublemaker! Sino ba yung nangangamkam ng teritoryo? Sino ba yung nagpapatayo ng mga artificial islands? Sino ba ang sumisira sa marine ecosystem? Sino yung nananakot sa ating mga mangingisda? Sino yung mga bumabangga sa ating mga vessels, vessels ng mga fishermen, vessels ng Navy and Philippine Coast Guard? And then tayo pa ang troublemaker? So I think there would be enough grounds, enough basis to declare him as persona non grata kapag hindi siya mag-apologize o bawiin yung kanyang mga sinabi [if he does not apologize or take back his words] at he would behave henceforth," she added.

(And then calling us a troublemaker in our own territory. We're the troublemaker? Who has been usurping territory? Who has been setting up artificial islands? Who has been destroying the marine ecosystem? Who has been threatening our fishermen? Who has been ramming into fishermen's boats and the vessels of the Navy and the Philippine Coast Guard? And then they call us the troublemaker?)

Last week, a social media post by Philippine Coast Guard spokesperson for the West Philippine Sea Rear Admiral Jay Tarriela showed Jing being interviewed where he said, "If we want to use force, we may easily win. But no, we will not use force. You know, we love peace, and in this region, we enjoy the peace."
Threat to ban

On China's threat to ban more Philippine government officials from its territory should the Chinese ambassador be declared persona non grata by the Philippines, de Lima said, "That is, of course, also their prerogative."

China has banned Defense Secretary Gilberto Teodoro Jr. and his family from entering China, including Hong Kong and Macau, claiming he had "repeatedly made erroneous remarks concerning China" which undermined China's "legitimate interests" and bilateral ties.
But she said Philippine government officials should not just keep silent about the Chinese ambassador's threats and demeanor.

"Bakit tayo ang mag-iingat sa sasabihin natin na sila palagi yung nag-uumpisa? And kapag meron akong isang post na sila ang nananakot sa atin, sila ang nagsasabi kung ano-ano tungkol sa Pilipinas. And then sila pa yung, at kung tayo ay nagpu-push back, babaligtarin nila ang naratibo," de Lima said.

(Why should we be the ones who should be careful about what we say when they are always the ones starting it? And when I post that they are the ones trying to intimidate us, they're the ones saying all these things about the Philippines. And when we push back, they try to flip the narrative.)

"So hindi naman pwede manahimik tayo habang naririnig at nakikita yung ganyang pag-uugali ng Chinese ambassador. Sila'y nagdi-disrespect sa international law dahil hindi nila kinikilala yung ruling ng Arbitral Tribunal na invalid supposedly yung nin-dash claim nila," she stated.

(So we cannot stay quiet while we can see and hear the behavior of the Chinese ambassador. They disrespect international law by refusing to recognize the ruling of the Arbitral Tribunal that their nine-dash claim is invalid.)
'Intersectionality'?
Bicol Saro Party-list Representative Terry Ridon, a member of the House Committee on Foreign Affairs, refused to be intimated by China's threats to ban Philippine government officials.

"Ang aming mensahe sa kanila, 'tsinong' tinakot ninyo? Hindi naman ito hindi pa nangyayari. Ginawa na ito laban kay Secretary Francis Tolentino, laban kay Secretary Gibo Teodoro. So kung gusto nilang gumawa ng dagdag pang listahan ng mga opisyal at tauhan na ipa-ban nila sa China ay gawin na nila yon ngayon," Ridon said.

(Our message to them is, who are you trying to frighten? It's not like this hasn't happened before. They did this to Secretary Francis Tolentino and Secretary Gibo Teodoro. So if they want to add to their list of officials and people to ban from China, they should do it already.)

Ridon, a member of the House Comm on Foreign Affairs, on China’s threat to ban more Phil govt officials: Tsinong tinakot nyo?… Kung gusto nilang gumawa ng dagdag pang listahan… gawin na nila yon ngayon. @gmanews @gmanewsbreaking https://t.co/wBZhVbA7v9— Tina PanganibanPerez (@tinapperez) October 19, 2026

Ridon added that he and other members of the House of Representatives will be filing a resolution to investigate the alleged "intersectionality ng propagandists ng Tsina sa bansa at ng mga supporters ng ating pamilya Duterte."
([The] intersectionality between the China propagandists and the Duterte family.)
Ridon said there were observations that those defending the Dutertes online are also defending China.

"Kasi pagka tinignan talaga natin yung kanilang social media output, dalawa lang po ang paksa - pagtatanggol sa mga Duterte, pagtatanggol sa Tsina. So magandang pag-aralan po ng Kongreso ito. kung kailangan pong wasakin itong network na ito, dapat din po yung gawin," he explained.

(If you look at their social media output, they have two topics: defending the Dutertes and defending China. So it would be good for Congress to investigate this, if thi snetwork needs to be taken down, what needs to be done.)
Ridon said he is set to file the resolution within the month.
The Makabayan Bloc, on the other hand, said cool heads must prevail as it called on all parties to "immediately de-escalate and return to the path of sober, principled diplomacy."

"As we continue to assert our sovereign rights and legal victory in the West Philippine Sea, we aver that diplomacy and peaceful resolution should be our main path," Act Teachers Party-list Representative Antonio Tinio, Gabriela Party-list Representaive Sarah Elago, and Kabataan Party-list Representative Renee Co said in a joint statement today. — BM, GMA News

articles.title: Cuts force World Food Programme to end support for half a million Palestinians in Gaza
articles.summary:
Two-thirds of population face crisis levels of food insecurity and 200,000 people are in danger of famine

This winter is likely to deepen hunger for Palestinians in Gaza, after sweeping aid…
articles.byline: Emma Graham-Harrison in Jerusalem and Seham Tantesh in Gaza

blocks.text: This winter is likely to deepen hunger for Palestinians in Gaza, after sweeping aid cuts forced the UN’s World Food Programme (WFP) to end support for more than half a million people each month, the agency’s director for Palestine said.
More than a year after a Trump-brokered ceasefire came into force, promised reconstruction has not begun, there are few jobs and the vast majority in Gaza still rely on aid to eat.
This summer, WFP programmes helped feed three-quarters of Gaza’s population, about 1.6 million people, but funding has fallen by more than half from 2025 levels.

blocks.caption: People receiving aid at the Egyptian camp in central Gaza, where thousands of displaced families live in tents.  Photograph: WFP/Jaber Badwan

blocks.text: As a result, from October, aid has been scaled back to 1.1 million people each month. Cuts to deliveries of ration boxes, cash stipends to buy food in markets, and hot meals at community kitchens have already been rolled out.
The WFP needs more than £300m over the next six months to restore and maintain critical programmes in Palestine.
A year of large aid shipments ended a famine declared in summer 2025 and reduced the most severe hunger, but without steps to rebuild Gaza’s economy, most families still rely on food handouts.

blocks.caption: Hot meals from community kitchens have only been delivered every other day in October.  Photograph: WFP Mohamed Hinnawi

blocks.text: “These are very fragile gains, easily reversed, and the situation is still brutal,” said Shaun Hughes, the WFP’s representative and country director for Palestine.

Two-thirds of the population in Gaza face crisis levels of food insecurity, phase three under the Integrated Food Security Phase Classification (IPC), which is used to assess if a population is approaching famine.

Food insecurity is at emergency levels for 200,000 Palestinians, which means immediate humanitarian supplies are needed to prevent deaths from hunger, Hughes said. This is IPC phase four, one step away from famine conditions.

Young children and their mothers are particularly vulnerable. After enduring years of food shortages, one in eight children in Gaza are chronically malnourished or stunted, a recent Unicef survey found, and may have suffered permanent damage.

blocks.caption: One in eight children in Gaza are chronically malnourished or stunted, a recent Unicef survey found.  Photograph: WFP Mohamed Hinnawi

blocks.text: Humanitarian aid will be needed at scale until Israel and the international community launch the large-scale reconstruction promised last year. There is no way for most people to feed their own families at present, because about 80% of Gaza’s population is unemployed, according to UN data.

“We need to invest in recovery. This humanitarian operation isn’t affordable or sustainable in the long term,” Hughes said. “Ultimately that’s also what everyone in Gaza is telling us. They really don’t want to be reliant on these handouts, don’t want to stand in the hot meals queue every day. They want to have some chance of stability and recovery.”

Gaza was self-sufficient in fruit and vegetables before the war, but the vast majority of farmland has been occupied by Israel’s military. The sophisticated greenhouse and irrigation systems that supported agricultural production have been destroyed.
Fish has historically been a key source of protein in the territory, but the Israeli navy bars fishing boats from waters off the coast.

blocks.caption: Sanaa lives with her husband and six daughters in a tent at the Egyptian camp: ‘Before the war, we could get whatever we needed.’  Photograph: WFP/Jaber Badwan

blocks.text: Alaa Sarhan, 40, lives with his wife and five children aged between four and 16 in a tent near the “yellow line” the marker of Israeli control. They have already noticed the impact of the WFP cuts.

“In recent days, we have had to plan our meals around what is available rather than what we want to eat,” he said. A former paramedic, he was injured by Israeli attacks nearly two decades ago, and his disability benefits buy very little.
“Often, I give up my share of food so my children can eat. I got accustomed to doing this because the most important thing is that they have something to eat.”

For three years, Israeli restrictions on aid shipments have been the main driver of hunger and malnutrition in Gaza. For months at a time, entry of food was restricted or entirely barred as Palestinians went hungry inside the territory.

Now, for the first time since October 2023, lack of funds may also become an obstacle to feeding hungry Palestinians. Israel’s controls on shipments into Gaza exacerbate funding shortfalls, because they make humanitarian work particularly expensive compared with other parts of the world.

blocks.caption: The cost of delivering aid is pushed up by the limited and expensive warehouse space because of the mass destruction of buildings.  Photograph: WFP/Mohamed Hinnawi

blocks.text: Limits on fuel, engine oil and spare parts, and complex, opaque shipping restrictions push up transport time and costs. Mass destruction of buildings by airstrikes means warehouse space is limited and costly.

Even an influx of cash might not allow the WFP to immediately reverse the cuts. Sourcing and shipping the ingredients for ration boxes can take about three months, and the reduction of cash transfers may already be affecting supply chains.

The injection of more than £30m a month has “underpinned purchasing power for the private sector in Gaza”, Hughes said, allowing trucks to come in with relatively expensive shipments of both healthy and unhealthy food.
For now, the WFP has tried to reduce the impact of funding cuts by scaling back these programmes rather than cutting them entirely. Families who get ration boxes will receive one, rather than two.

blocks.caption: The WHP’s ration boxes and flour give families essential supplies to prepare meals and bake bread.  Photograph: WFP/Jaber Badwan

blocks.text: But even limited reductions may push families with no other food source or income back into dangerous levels of malnutrition. For the poorest of the poor, reduced rations don’t work, Hughes said. “There’s only so far you can cut [support] until you don’t have the food security impact at the household level.”

The WFP is trying to monitor hunger levels so they reach the most vulnerable, monitoring “negative coping strategies”. These include whether people have skipped meals, or are seeking exploitative and dangerous work.

Nesreen Muqayed, 50, lives with her husband, four children and two grandchildren. She needs a regular diet to manage kidney problems, and a grandson who is on the autism spectrum cannot tolerate many foods.

Despite these urgent medical needs, they often go hungry. “Sometimes we try to save part of a meal for breakfast because we do not know whether we will have anything to eat the following day,” Muqayed said. “The situation has become more difficult over the past two weeks.”
The hot meals from community kitchens that make up a large part of their diet have only been delivered every other day in October, and their meagre backup supplies are already running out.

“I used the last of our flour yesterday,” she said. Beyond grappling with daily hunger, she also finds it painful denying her children healthy food they want and need for their development, because they cannot even afford bananas.

“Sometimes I pass a fruit seller and look at what he has on display, but I do not have the money to buy,” she said. “Fruit and vegetables have become luxuries that we cannot afford regularly, even though they are basic necessities that every family should be able to access.”

articles.title: For Pru Life UK’s Cecille Marano, Filipinos deserve ‘peace of mind’
articles.summary: Just like Pru Life UK, the vice president for corporate performance management marks her 30th year of providing Filipinos with protection

blocks.text: Photography by Lem Atienza; makeup by Dorothy Mamalio; hair by Marjorie Caballos
Just like Pru Life UK, the vice president for corporate performance management marks her 30th year of providing Filipinos with protection

items: Cecille Marano reflects on her 30-year journey with Pru Life UK, highlighting the company's growth from a new player to a market leader in the insurance industry.
Marano emphasizes the importance of integrity, trust, and empathy in her role, wishing for the company to continue providing accessible insurance and fostering financial literacy in the future.

blocks.text: This is AI-generated. Read the article for full context. Report any errors.

Editor’s note: This content is sponsored by Pru Life UK and was handled by BrandRap, the sales and marketing arm of Rappler. No member of the news and editorial team participated in the publishing of this piece.
September 16, 1996. There isn’t a single lull in Cecille Marano’s train of thought when remembering her first day at Pru Life UK.

“Pru Life UK was a new industry player back then,” she recalled their old office in Makati where office chairs and tables filled every available space as employees and agents alike were crammed together in a single floor. They had to make do with an open setup type of office until things could be sorted out in a more orderly fashion.

blocks.caption: A glimpse of Marano’s life with Pru Life UK

blocks.text: “Zero to One” is how Marano would describe the company’s evolution story. She said that Pru Life UK started from scratch. It did not acquire nor sought partnerships with local insurance companies and relied solely on organic growth.

“5 in 5” was the slogan of the strategic campaign to leapfrog Pru Life UK among the top 5 insurance companies in terms of new business within its first 5 years of operations. Remarkably, it successfully breached into the top 5 group on the 4th year.

Competition continues to be tough in an industry long dominated by traditional players. Still, through persistence and unrelenting effort, Pru Life UK ultimately garnered the coveted Top 1 position in 2020 and retained market leadership as of 2025.

Over the last 30 years, Cecille witnessed how the company’s transformed from a budding new player to an industry leader. She also recalls how the company deftly navigated the Asian financial crises in 1997, the 2008 global financial meltdown, and the global recession in the wake of the COVID-19 pandemic.

Despite these headwinds, the company rapidly expanded market share just as the agency force grew by leaps and bounds. Today, Pru Life UK boasts of the largest sales force with more than 33,000 agents.
Her first day at Pru Life UK soon turned into 30 years – which is also celebrating its 30th year of business operations in the Philippines this 2026.

blocks.caption: Photography by Lem Atienza; makeup by Dorothy Mamalio; hair by Marjorie Caballos

blocks.text: Marano, who currently serves as Pru Life UK’s vice president for corporate performance management, spends most of her week reviewing and analyzing vital financial data. She regularly coordinates with business owners for performance updates on key initiatives along with finalizing reports.

Wednesdays are often reserved for her team’s weekly engagement: discussing status and progress of deliverables, addressing new issues, time-sensitive work requirements considered as top priority, and projects for endorsement to the chief strategy officer, among others.

She attributes her long tenure with the company to the shared sense of purpose, passion, conviction and collective commitment of all employees in achieving the company’s goals and vision along with adherence to its core values.
If summed up to three words, Marano describes Pru Life UK’s employee culture with verbs, not adjectives: “listening, understanding, and delivering.”

Interestingly, these words also align with the company’s core values, showing how Marano has their vision and mission down pat. It also helps that she personally carries values that don’t stray away from what the company stands for.

“Integrity, trustworthiness, and empathy are the key principles that I embrace. I do believe in being truthful and transparent in dealing with everybody. It allows me to build a genuine and solid relationship with my colleagues,” she said, adding that these traits also help her to listen to people’s concerns effectively, which enables her to provide proper inputs to help them make sound decisions.

blocks.caption: Photography by Lem Atienza; makeup by Dorothy Mamalio; hair by Marjorie Caballos

blocks.text: After all, it’s always been about enabling Filipinos to think and act to achieve lifetime financial security.

But while there is a growing awareness and even desire among Filipinos to learn more about insurance, it can’t be denied that many still view it as an afterthought expense rather than a necessity. For Marano, Pru Life UK has actively worked on this by fostering financial literacy among ordinary Filipinos.
“Pru Life UK was the first to introduce the Variable Unit-Linked in the Philippines. It offered added flexibility for clients to buy insurance products with an investment element,” she explains.
Their financial literacy efforts also involve education at the grassroots level, engaging with government agencies and educators, and teaching school children the basic concepts of money and finance.
Now that Marano has served her 30th year with Pru Life UK, what does she wish for the company for its next 30 years?

“I wish to see the company continue to provide accessible and relevant insurance products to Filipino families and further intensify financial literacy efforts at the grassroots level.” She adds, “I also wish that Pru Life UK would continue to earn the trust of Filipino families and help them ultimately achieve financial freedom and the peace of mind that comes along with it.

blocks.caption: A glimpse of Marano’s life with Pru Life UK

blocks.text: As a matter of fact, she considers “peace of mind” as closely associated with “protection” – the core of what Pru Life UK’s services are about, from health and critical illness coverage to investment-linked protection plans.

“For me, protection engenders peace of mind,” she says. “Filipino families have peace of mind knowing that they are financially prepared for uncertainties; agents have peace of mind and a sense of fulfillment in helping Filipino families secure their future; and employees have peace of mind and a sense of satisfaction safeguarding the future of Filipino families.”
And there’s no better testament to this than Marano’s story – which has always been filled with full-circle moments.

Cecille Marano caps off the interview by saying, “It is a great honor and privilege to serve and be part of Pru Life UK’s stellar journey over the last three decades and counting. I am truly blessed and grateful to Pru Life UK that helps me protect and provide for my family.” – Rappler.com

Hello and welcome to the US politics live blog.
Donald Trump will attend a campaign rally in Kansas later today, where incumbent Republican Senator Roger Marshall is in an unexpectedly close race with Democrat Adam Hamilton.
Marshall’s medical billing scandal is threatening to erode his support, though he is still favored to win.
Hamilton, the founder of the largest Methodist congregation in the US, won in a crowded Democratic primary earlier this year.

Hamilton won 35% of the vote in the 11-candidate Democratic primary. His campaign announced he had broken a quarterly fundraising record in the state, and two major election forecasters say the Senate race has grown more competitive since Hamilton won his party’s primary.
Kansas has not elected a Democrat to the Senate since 1932, and more than half a century has passed since one of their nominees even came close.

articles.title: Deadly fire at Canada military base moved a kilometre 'in 30 to 60 seconds'
articles.summary: The blaze that killed four men and injured dozens of others spread with alarming speed, accounts suggest.

blocks.text: The fire that killed four members of the Canadian military and injured dozens of others on Saturday spread with alarming speed, accounts suggest.
It broke out in a grassy training area at a base in the province of Alberta and spread rapidly due to strong winds.

"The fire was 1km (0.6 miles) away when the wind shifted," said Maj-Gen Wade Rutland, commander of the 1st Canadian Division of the Canadian Armed Forces. "It is not normal for a fire to move a kilometre in 30 to 60 seconds."

Prime Minister Mark Carney described it as "one of the worst tragedies for the forces on Canadian soil in peacetime". Officials have ruled out the possibility of "any terrorist activity" being to blame for the fire.
The blaze began at about 16:00 (22:00 GMT) on Saturday at Canadian Forces Base Wainwright, one of the country's busiest military training bases.
The BBC has confirmed that Sgt Morgan Wong, Pte Shaun Farrell, Pte Aidan Goulding and Pte Hayden Lykkemark have died.
Of the 39 injured people receiving care in hospital, at least 19 are in a critical condition.

Warren Thirsk, an emergency department doctor at the Royal Alexandra Hospital, told Canadian broadcaster CBC that the number of patients involved in the incident had "completely overwhelmed" healthcare facilities in Wainwright.
In account of Saturday's events, Rutland told reporters that members of the infantry had been conducting "high-intensity combat training with live munitions" at a grenade range and attack range.
He told reporters that officials knew about the fire on the base for several hours, but it was decided that training "could carry on for a certain amount of time".
"I spoke to my commander last night, and he said within 30 seconds to a minute they saw no fire, and then there was a fire right on top of them," Rutland said.
Rutland said it was not yet known what exactly caused the fire.

Some witnesses had said they had heard explosions, fuelling speculation that oil and gas infrastructure may have been hit and sparked the fire. But Rutland said authorities "do not believe this [incident] to be a result of any oil and gas infrastructure".
The Canadian Armed Forces has said that "while the incident remains under investigation, at this time, there are no indications that it was the result of any terrorist activity".
Forecasters had issued a wind warning on Saturday for large parts of Alberta, predicting wind gusts of up to 90km/h (66mph), Canadian broadcaster CBS said.
According to Rutland, the investigation may take at least a month.

Wainwright, about 130 miles east of Edmonton, Alberta's capital, is one of the main bases used by the Canadian military for live-fire training exercises, and it houses troops from Canada and allied countries.
About 690 military personnel and 300 civilian workers are on site on a typical day.

articles.title: Teodoro: China's aggression threatens other South China Sea claimants, too
articles.summary: China"s maritime aggression threatens not only the Philippines but also other Southeast Asian countries with territorial claims in the South China Sea, Defense Secretary Gilberto Teodoro Jr. said on…

blocks.text: Published October 19, 2026 5:37pm

China’s maritime aggression threatens not only the Philippines but also other Southeast Asian countries with territorial claims in the South China Sea, Defense Secretary Gilberto Teodoro Jr. said on Monday.

During the Senate Committee on Finance’s deliberations on the Department of National Defense’s (DND) proposed P324.632-billion budget for 2027, Sen. Erwin Tulfo asked Teodoro how the department was preparing to address threats from Beijing amid tensions in the areas that the Philippines calls the West Philippine Sea.
“We are doing our best to work not only on our own but also with our allies to deter any further aggressive military action by China,” Teodoro said.

“It’s not only a threat to us, but it is also a threat to Vietnam, to Malaysia, and to Brunei; and a threat to Japan, where their actions are equally aggressive, not to the extent we are facing,” he added.
Tulfo raised the matter amid recent remarks by the Chinese ambassador to the Philippines that Filipino officials had viewed as a veiled threat against the country.
“What preparations are you making now to counter these threats and allay the fears of the public? Na bobombahin tayo, dudurugin, etc. (We will be bombed, crushed, etc.),” Tulfo asked.
Teodoro said the Philippine government was working closely with its allies to deter further aggressive actions by China.
He stressed the importance of building deterrence to discourage China from taking further aggressive action, while urging the Philippines and its allies to carefully consider their responses.
“Ang dapat nating gawin ay to build deterrence. Magdalawang isip muna, kahit sino bago tayo guluhin. Kasi maaring pasakitin natin ulo nila and it's not worth it at the end of the day,” he said.
(What we need to do is build deterrence so that anyone would think twice before provoking us. We could give them a headache, and it's not worth it in the end.)
China claims most of the South China Sea, parts of which are also claimed by the Philippines, Brunei, Malaysia, Taiwan, Vietnam and Indonesia.
In 2016, an arbitral tribunal in The Hague ruled in favor of the Philippines, finding that China had no legal basis to claim historic rights to resources within the so-called nine-dash line.
Also on Monday, the Department of Foreign Affairs (DFA) summoned Chinese Ambassador Jing Quan to convey the Philippines’ “serious concern and strong objection” to his recent remarks.
Jing had claimed that China would “easily win” if it resorted to force in the West Philippine Sea.
Teodoro reiterated the DND’s rejection of the Chinese ambassador’s accusations against the Philippines.

“Consistent with our earlier pronouncements, number one, we refute all allegations made by the ambassador that we are troublemakers and are provoking. Inuulit namin ang aming pagsuporta, pagtaguyod sa UNCLOS at sa UN charter,” he said.
(We reiterate our support for and commitment to upholding the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea and the United Nations Charter.)— MCG, GMA News

articles.title: China’s economy grows faster than forecast after AI boom boosts exports
articles.summary: Third-quarter GDP up by 4.5% compared with last year as industrial output is buoyed by electronics demand

blocks.text: Roaring exports lifted China’s economic growth in the third quarter of this year, with factory output growing much faster than consumer spending.

China’s GDP grew by 4.5% year-on-year between July and September, the National Bureau of Statistics of China reported on Monday. The figures were better than economists had expected and up from the second quarter’s growth rate of 4.3%.
China’s economy has now grown by 4.6% in the first nine months of the year, putting it on track to hit the government’s 2026 target of 4.5%-5% growth without extra stimulus measures.
Industrial production rose 5.5% in September, up from 5.2% in August, while retail sales only increased 1.1%, up from 0.4%.

Duncan Wrigley, the chief China economist at Pantheon Macroeconomics, said Beijing’s policymakers were likely to conclude that their efforts to stabilise headline growth in the third quarter were successful.

“Headline industrial production rose in September partly as coalmines resumed operations after safety inspections prompted by a major accident. Manufacturing output growth remained robust at 6.0% year on year in September, buoyed up by stronger export demand for electronics, AI-related equipment and autos,” Wrigley said.
“Hi-tech manufacturing output continues to outperform traditional sectors, as China climbs the value-added ladder,” Wrigley added.
However, fixed-asset investment fell 7.2% over the first nine months, property investment tumbled by 20.6%, and infrastructure spending remained weak.
Data last week showed that China’s exports surged by more than a third in September, lifted by a rise in shipments of electronics related to AI.

“This pickup in GDP growth mainly reflects ongoing export strength on the global AI/tech boom, more than offsetting drags from the Iran conflict and ongoing weakness in domestic demand,” said analysts at ABN Amro.

articles.title: Alberta heads to polls to decide whether to hold vote on separation from Canada
articles.summary: Polling suggests most Albertans favour remaining part of the country, although the debate alone has proven divisive.

blocks.text: People in the province of Alberta head to the polls on Monday to decide whether to hold a referendum at a later date on separating from Canada.

The vote was called earlier this year by the leader of the province, Danielle Smith, after a grassroots group gathered about 300,000 signatures on a petition that asked for a binding referendum on separation.
Many of those who support separation say the oil-rich province's economic growth has been stifled by the environmental policies of Canada's central government in Ottawa.
But those who want Alberta to remain part of Canada - who include Prime Minister Mark Carney - have called for the country to show unity in the face of external pressures.
Polls have suggested that the majority of Albertans would vote to remain in Canada, though the pre-vote debate alone has proven divisive.
Another group collected signatures for its own petition that opposed separation, which was signed by more than 400,000 people. The province's population is about five million people.
If Albertans do vote on Monday to move ahead with a binding referendum, that could happen as soon as 2027, Smith has said.

Smith's decision to allow Monday's vote came in spite of the fact that a court blocked the pro-separation petition, saying it failed to consult indigenous First Nations whose land would be affected if the province separated from Canada.
Following the judge's ruling, First Nations groups have branded Smith's decision to allow the voting process to play out as "undemocratic" and "authoritarian".

Smith, the leader of the United Conservative Party of Alberta (UCP), has defended her decision to put the issue to voters. She opposes separation herself, but says the process gives the province's residents a chance to have their say on the issue.

The key question on the voting paper will ask: "Should Alberta remain a province of Canada or should the Government of Alberta commence the legal process required under the Canadian Constitution to hold a binding provincial referendum on whether or not Alberta should separate from Canada?"

The separatist movement is led by Mitch Sylvestre, a gun shop owner from the town of Bonnyville, and Jeffrey Rath, a lawyer based in Calgary. They are both members of a group called the Alberta Prosperity Project, which argues that the province's economic growth has been hindered by years of Liberal party rule in Ottawa.

Successive Liberal governments of the last 10 years have put environmental policies above helping Alberta develop its oil and gas sector, they argue. They say Alberta would get to keep more of its wealth if it splits from Canada.

Chris Scott, founder of pro-separatist group Let's Talk Alberta, told BBC News on the eve of the poll that the campaign had already achieved some of its goals, regardless of what happened on Monday. "The key is the conversation has started and it needs to continue," he said. "What's started can't be stopped now," he added.

Those who oppose separation say a newly independent Alberta would be left responsible for billions of dollars in debt. They warn that the uncertainty - which they liken to the UK's Brexit vote to leave the European Union in 2016 - would drive thousands of jobs and investment out of the province.
Carney has called on voters to deliver a decisive vote against separation. Speaking at a rally on Thursday, he warned that the stakes were high.

"The world has become more dangerous and divided. Some outside our borders are working to break us so they can own us," Carney said, echoing warnings he has made in the past about his country's ongoing trade war with the United States.
Alongside the separation question, Albertans will vote on nine other issues - a number of which focus on whether the province should have more control over its immigration system.
Hundreds of thousands of people had voted early by post ahead of Monday, and early figures suggested a strong voter turnout.
The province's election officials will count the ballots by hand, and have 48 hours to complete the task - starting from no earlier than 20:00 local time on Monday (02:00 GMT on Tuesday).
The key question, on separation, will be counted in its entirety first. Officials have said results should be available in the early hours of Tuesday.

articles.title: Why did 3 SET senator-members favor Erwin Tulfo’s ouster?
articles.summary: 'Justice and fairness went out of the window when three minority senator-members voted in favor of an out-of-time motion for reconsideration filed by a petitioner without legal standing,' says…

blocks.text: ERWIN TULFO. Senator Erwin Tulfo pushes for stronger protections for persons with disability (PWDs) during the hearing of the Committee on Social Justice, Welfare and Rural Development on Monday, October 19, 2026.
Senate of the Philippines

'Justice and fairness went out of the window when three minority senator-members voted in favor of an out-of-time motion for reconsideration filed by a petitioner without legal standing,' says Senator Ping Lacson

The Senate Electoral Tribunal’s (SET) decision to affirm the dismissal of a petition to unseat Senator Erwin Tulfo over alleged citizenship issues was largely anticipated — the March ruling was anchored on insufficiency in form — but the votes of three senator-members favoring Tulfo’s ouster was not.

In a statement signed by SET Secretary Luis Jose Geronimo, the tribunal said it denied the motion for reconsideration (MR) filed by petitioner Berteni Causing, seeking to reverse its March 2 ruling summarily dismissing his quo warranto petition for being “insufficient in form.”
The SET said the MR was filed beyond the prescribed period and “failed to comply with the filing and service requirements of the 2020 SET Rules.”

The nine-member tribunal convened at the Senate on Friday, October 16, with the Supreme Court (SC) justices and senator-members in attendance. Six SET members voted to deny the MR, while three opposed the dismissal, reportedly minority senators Robin Padilla, Pia Cayetano, and Camille Villar.

SC Senior Associate Justice Marvic Leonen chairs the SET, with SC justices Henri Jean Paul Inting and Ramon Paul Hernando serving as members. Senators Kiko Pangilinan, Bam Aquino, and Lito Lapid represent the majority bloc in the tribunal while Padilla, Cayetano, and Villar represent the Senate minority.

“Let’s give credit to the three SC justice-members and the other three senator-members who undoubtedly knew the obvious procedural flaw which resulted in a 6-3 vote, thus dismissing the MR,” Senator Panfilo “Ping” Lacson said over the weekend.
Lacson, without naming the three minority senators, questioned their decision to favor what he described as an “out-of-time MR filed by a petitioner without legal standing.”

“Justice and fairness went out of the window when three minority senator-members voted in favor of an out-of-time motion for reconsideration filed by a petitioner without legal standing,” Lacson said in a social media post.
“Their motive may be deeper than personal issues against Sen Tulfo,” he added.
Tulfo has repeatedly clashed with minority senators in the months spanning Alan Peter Cayetano’s tumultuous Senate presidency, the subsequent leadership change, and the ongoing impeachment trial.

In June, Tulfo called out then-Senate president Alan, calling him “thick-skinned” for skipping Senate session for a second consecutive day, along with minority senators, preventing the upper chamber from holding sessions due to a lack of quorum. At the time, Cayetano said they would not attend the session to keep control of the Senate blue ribbon committee and other panels.

During the impeachment trial, Tulfo questioned whether the proceedings were the proper venue for senator-judges to discuss their personal legal issues. This came after Padilla denied allegations that he had ignored an Ombudsman order related to complaints accusing him of obstruction of justice.
Tulfo also figured in a heated exchange with Villar during a debate on whether to revisit the threshold for convicting an impeachable official.

Villar took offense and became emotional when she defended colleagues from Tulfo’s remarks that the framers of the 1987 Constitution did not anticipate that future senator-judges could face corruption-related cases, such as plunder and theft.
Asked to comment on the 6-3 vote at the SET, Tulfo did not confirm the names of those who voted against him but said he was “hurt.”

“We were hurt. As you can see, we were all interacting with each other and then suddenly, they will do that. We’re a bit sad but that is their right. I mean, what can we do?… Kung ‘yun ang pananaw nila, then so be it. Ipagpasa-Diyos na lamang natin (If that is their view, then so be it. I leave it up to God),” he said in an interview on Monday, October 19.
Tulfo was more candid on Facebook, where he shared an editorial illustration depicting himself being stabbed in the back by knife-wielding arms labeled “Sens. Padilla, Villar, Pia.”
“Nakita ko lang (I just saw this)…. tsk, tsk, tsk,” he said in his post on Saturday, October 17.
What other “deeper motive” could there be, as suggested by Lacson? Where could a senator’s removal from office have any significant impact?

If one were to consider the impeachment trial, had the SET removed Tulfo from office, the number of active senator-judges participating in the trial would have fallen to 19. Based on the denominator, 15 votes would have been needed to convict Duterte, while five votes would have resulted in her acquittal. – Rappler.com

articles.title: Teodoro seeks higher capital outlay for 2027 to boost defense coverage
articles.summary: The Department of National Defense (DND) on Monday is seeking higher capital outlay under its 2027 budget as it seeks to build additional infrastructure that would bolster the country"s security…

blocks.text: Published October 19, 2026 5:14pm

The Department of National Defense (DND) on Monday is seeking higher capital outlay under its 2027 budget as it seeks to build additional infrastructure that would bolster the country’s security capabilities.

The National Expenditure Program provides for a P324.632 billion budget for the Defense Dept. next year. Of which, P32,671,776 is allotted for capital outlay, a decline from the P43,148,125 approved for this year.
Defense Secretary Gilberto Teodoro Jr. said that the capital outlay is the armed forces’ “biggest gap.”

“We need a lot of infrastructure right now, particularly on the eastern sea board, where we do not have naval presence. We do not have substantial infrastructure in Palawan, not for the naval purposes, but for the army purposes, which will serve as hubs for supporting our strategic bases,” he told the Senate Committee on Finance during the budget deliberations.
The defense chief also noted that there is only one Army brigade for the province of Mindoro and a single infantry division to secure Northern Luzon.

“So we really need to refocus our strategic positioning in these areas and we cannot do that until, sustainably, until the Army solidifies its footprint in the Philippines,” said Tedoro. “So capital outlay is extremely important also for building critical infrastructure facilities for security of our platforms and security of our operations.”
Moreover, Teodoro said the DND is eyeing building hubs in various parts of the country to help the defense forces’ mobility.
“So our mobility is sacrificed. We cannot bridge the whole of the Philippines, but the best we can do is to provide hubs, as many hubs as possible, which will support sustained operations,” he said.
Further, the department expressed its interest to have reserves for oil products.

“We are busy building up our reserve, not only in terms of ammunition, but we need it also in terms of petroleum, oil, and lubricants. We have big notional amounts of petroleum ready, but if we do not have physical custody of this, we will be relying on private gas stations to serve our needs, which is a vulnerability of our operating troops,” said Teodoro. —RF, GMA News

articles.title: Three months of experience with an ergonomic vertical mouse
articles.summary: If you get wrist strains, this could be up your alley

blocks.text: All of my previous mice were cheap, wired, office mice. One of them succumbed to pandemic-era Minecraft gameplay. While I was using its replacement, I heard about vertical mice: uniquely fin-shaped peripherals that allegedly cure desk-worker wrist strain.

My wrist hurt when I held my mouse the normal way, so I took a leaf out of this and started holding them from the side… as much as I was able. Eventually, my last mouse started ghost-clicking, and I wanted to see if shaking hands with a real vertical mouse was the ergonomic miracle it claims to be.

So I grabbed a knowledgeable friend, checked out online resources, and bought a promisingly named Go Comfy W195R from Fantech. And three months into using this mouse, my wrist and hand are much happier.

Relax your arms and drop them to your side: your palms will face your body. If you drop your relaxed arms on a desk, your palms will be perpendicular to the surface. Sure, you could twist your wrist to make your palm lie flat, like you would for a typical mouse, but maintaining that for a long time will keep you in an unnatural position.

A vertical mouse is built off your natural arm posture by having its body on the side rather than the top. This structure allows you to grip the mouse from the side, retain your palm’s curve, and keep your wrist untwisted.

The Fantech Go Comfy W195R is designed just like that. I got used to the shape quickly not just because it felt comfortable, but also because I was already holding mice like this. My pointer finger appreciates not having to stretch to reach the left click. At approximately 114 grams, the Go Comfy W195R is slightly heavier than my previous mouse, though it didn’t feel too different.

The mouse fits the shape of my hand well, and my wrist doesn’t ache anymore. My thumb, on the other hand, gets a mild strain if on the thumb rest for too long, which I’ve resolved by resting it above the side buttons and giving my hand a break. I’ll take that over my poor wrist.

All my previous mice were wired mice, so I didn’t have to charge or replace batteries. The Go Comfy W195R, however, is exclusively a wireless or Bluetooth connection. At first, I was sad to lose the convenience of being able to just plug it in, but I see the appeal of wireless now. There’s less clutter on my desk, and I can hold my mouse as near or as far as I like. I can even use my mouse from my couch.

I prefer to use my mouse wirelessly with the USB dongle, but I can also quickly switch it to the Bluetooth connection. In one moment, I could use it on my laptop, then I can toggle Bluetooth and connect it to my tablet.

The mouse uses an optical sensor, whose red light dims when it detects it’s no longer on a working surface. I’ve been flashed by my previous mice’s optical sensors when I held them up, so I find this to be a nice touch.
The left and right buttons are noticeably softer and silent, but the side buttons are clickier.

The plastic upper half of the mouse where the buttons are gathers dirt easily. When I run my finger over it, I can feel specks of dirt and dust, so I have to clean and wipe it frequently. It can be a bit annoying, but I see this as a bit of a silver lining: it reminds me to keep my mouse clean. I didn’t feel specks on my previous mice, so I dread to think of how dirty they actually were.

I’m right-handed, and my mouse is definitely for a right-handed person because of where the main buttons are. If you’re left-handed and looking for a vertical mouse, note that while left-handed vertical mice do exist, they’re harder to find.

I’ve shown my mouse to other people with different hands, and while my mouse fits my small hand, it does not fit bigger hands. I got lucky here as I neglected to check the size of the mouse before buying. This is a bit hard to check online since you can’t hold it, but online listings should show the dimensions.

Lastly, these ergonomic mice are built to strain you less while you use them, but they won’t stop strains entirely nor are the sole source of your strains. Be sure to have proper posture and to take breaks and stretch regularly.
If a vertical mouse suits you, here’s where you can buy it. – Rappler.com

This piece was written by Rappler intern Czarina Yasmin Sia. Czarina is an earnest creator whose works focuses on the little things and helping others. She enjoys engaging with unconventional ways to tells stories and is eager to write about life’s overlooked aspects. A graduating Communication Arts student from De La Salle University Manila, she aims to inspire people to find wonder.

articles.title: Possible wreckage of Amelia Earhart's plane likely to be trees, say researchers
articles.summary: Researchers travelled to a remote Pacific Island to confirm whether an object first spotted on satellite imagery in 2020 solved the mystery of the pilot's disappearance.

blocks.text: Image source, Archaeological Legacy Institute
A satellite image of the so-called Taraia Object, which some had hypothesised could have been Amelia Earhart's plane, in a lagoon on Nikumaroro
Researches looking at what they thought could have been the wreckage of Amelia Earhart's plane on a remote Pacific island say it is likely to be washed up trees.

The team travelled to a lagoon in the Taraia Peninsula on Nikumaroro, Kiribati, to confirm whether a shiny object first spotted on satellite imagery in 2020 solved the decades-long mystery of the pioneering pilot's disappearance.
But Purdue University, which has a leading role in the study, said the so-called Taraia Object "was likely a collection of large trees deposited along the peninsula's sandspit".
By the time the team arrived at the site a good portion of the debris had fragmented and washed away, leaving only a single Y-shaped segment, the university said.

blocks.caption: Image caption, Amelia Earhart disappeared over the Pacific Ocean while piloting her Electra plane in 1937

blocks.text: Image source, Getty Images
Amelia Earhart disappeared over the Pacific Ocean while piloting her Electra plane in 1937

Images of the Taraia Object - which Purdue University said was visible in photography dating back to 1938 - led researchers to wonder if it was the remnants of a small aircraft sitting in shallow waters.
"This mystery has been ongoing for 90 years and the mystery continues," said project director Rick Pettigrew, speaking from near the site of the object.
"The island has been holding on to its secrets and it continues to do so. I think eventually someone will find conclusive evidence here," he added.

blocks.caption: A satellite image of Nikumaroro Island in the Pacific Ocean showing the location of the Taraia Object

blocks.text: Earhart's plane vanished without a trace in 1937 on the third-to-last leg of her attempt to fly around the world.
She had already successfully flown from California across South America, Africa and Asia in her twin-engine Lockheed Electra when she arrived in Lae, Papua New Guinea.
Earhart and her navigator Fred Noonan had planned to then travel towards Hawaii before returning to California.
But their plane vanished while trying to reach Howland Island, a remote uninhabited coral island about 400 miles (644km) from Nikumaroro, to refuel.
One theory is Earhart unintentionally navigated to Nikumaroro, where she ditched her plane and died a castaway.
The research team had travelled for five days by sea to reach Nikumaroro and was forced to spend several days on their ship following rough seas and strong winds, delaying their search on the island.
They spent four days onshore investigating the site.

blocks.caption: Map showing the relative locations of Papua New Guinea, Hawaii, Australia, Howland Island and Kikumaroro Island

articles.title: Safety concerns mount over Japan’s traditional festivals after string of fatal accidents
articles.summary:
Deputy mayor of Saijo died after becoming trapped under float, days after two similar incidents elsewhere

There is mounting concern over the safety of Japan’s traditional festivals after the…

blocks.text: There is mounting concern over the safety of Japan’s traditional festivals after the death of a senior local official who was reportedly crushed beneath a float at the weekend, days after two men died in similar incidents in another part of the country.

Akihiro Nabae, the deputy mayor of Saijo, in western Japan, was carrying a giant float with other participants in a festival on Saturday when he became trapped beneath the structure, Agence France-Presse reported. Nabae, 62, was taken to hospital and later pronounced dead, local media said, adding that no one else was injured.

He died less than two weeks after a 51-year-old man was crushed beneath a wooden float he was riding at one of the annual Danjiri festivals held in southern Osaka prefecture. The same day, a 48-year-old man was killed in a similar accident at a Danjiri event in a nearby town. Police said 16 people were injured in the incidents.

blocks.caption: Participants push and pull a float during the Danjiri festival celebrations in Anan, Tokushima. Photograph: Keiichi Miyashita/AFLO/Shutterstock

blocks.text: The accidents occurred when the floats, which can weigh up to 4 tonnes, toppled as they were being pulled at speed around tight corners by hundreds of men, police said. The turns, known as yarimawashi, are a highlight of the festivals, originally held to pray for good autumn harvests.
It is not clear if Nabae lost his balance or if the contraption toppled on to him, according to police in Saijo, where the festival has been held annually since the Edo period (1603-1868).
Media reports said 11 floats, each weighing as much as 3 tonnes, were lined up side by side at the time of the accident.
The annual Saijo festivals, featuring more than 100 floats, are held to thank Shinto deities for plentiful grain crops, the Jiji news agency said.

blocks.caption: The floats weigh up to 4 tonnes each. Photograph: Keiichi Miyashita/AFLO/Shutterstock

blocks.text: Saijo’s mayor, Mitsuyoshi Ochi, voiced shock and sadness at Nabae’s death. “Just when we were about to work together to build a new administration for Saijo, this tragedy occurred. I still can’t believe it. I offer my heartfelt condolences,” he said in a statement.

In February, two people died in a crush at the “naked man festival” in Okayama, where as many as 10,000 men dressed in fundoshi loincloths squeeze into the grounds of a temple and compete to seize a pair of sacred wooden sticks thrown into the crowd by the head priest. The two men who succeed are declared “lucky men” for the year.

articles.title: Need a document notarized? Supreme Court launches online service
articles.summary: The public can now notarize their documents online through three accredited platforms.

blocks.text: October 19, 2026 | 5:01pm
The logo of the Supreme Court at the Supreme Court Building in Manila.
Philstar.com / Ian Laqui
MANILA, Philippines — Electronic notarization (e-notarization) was officially launched by the Supreme Court on Monday, October 19.
According to the Supreme Court, the public can now notarize their documents online through three accredited platforms.
The accredited platforms are as follows:

items: Twala
QLegal
NotarizeIT

blocks.text: For any platform, one must prepare:

items: A valid, unexpired Philippine National ID or government-issued ID.
A working device with a camera and microphone.
A stable internet connection of at least 2 Mbps per user.
An up-to-date browser such as Chrome, Edge, Safari, or Firefox.
The document in PDF or PDF/A format.
An email address for account creation and platform notifications.

blocks.text: A person seeking e-notarization must also disable their VPN, proxy, or Tor, as these can interfere with location verification.

The validity of each electronically notarized document has the same "validity, force, and effect and may be relied upon to the same extent as any other notarial act performed under the 2004 Notarial Rules."
However, electronic notarization does not apply to the execution of documents that require wet signatures, according to the Rules of Electronic Notarization.
Examples of these documents include notarial wills, depositions, and paper documents and instruments with wet signatures or marks.

A person seeking electronic notarization also cannot use ordinary Zoom, Google Meet, or Microsoft Teams for the notarization itself; the act must be performed through a Supreme Court-accredited e-notarization platform.
Specific requirements for each platform can be accessed on the Supreme Court website.
